Sara K.: Heads up — saw a latency spike on canary-11 after the runtime patch. p50 up ~10ms for seqlen=512 workloads. Looks like kernel_decider flipped to a different Flash path mid-request for some head_dim=20 models.

Mike L.: Can you paste the profiler snapshot and the kernel decision log? which model / arch?

Sara K.: repro steps below, happened on sm90 nodes. quick log snippet:
```
[2026-03-18T10:12:03Z] request_id=abc123 model=redwood/v0.9 head_dim=20 seqlen=512 causal=true sm_arch=sm90
kernel_decider: evaluated_candidates=[flash_v3_causal, flash_v1_causal, sdpa_fast]
kernel_decider: chosen=flash_v1_causal score=0.62 reason="padbucketized:512->512; prefetch_est=on; kv_state=warmup"
latency_ms: before=18.2 after=28.4
```

Sara K.: repro command: `rb-runtime profile --node canary-11 --trace kernel_decider --qps 50 --payload seqlen=512,head_dim=20,causal=1`

Jordan: Hm. padbucketizer thresholds were adjusted in the patch — 512 fell into a boundary where we prefer the older v1 causal kernel because it avoids a prefetch path that was regressing for small head multiples. head_dim=20 is suspicious: our head-slice tiling heuristics expect multiples of 8 and sometimes treat 20 as "unaligned" which pushes fallback.

Aisha: Also saw KV-cache warmup interplay on the runs: first few tokens trigger different microbatching and prefetch flags. That plus head_dim aliasing can flip the kernel pick at token ~4 which explains mid-request jitter.

Mike L.: Can we add hysteresis to the kernel_decider so we don't flip mid-request? Something like: if a given (model, node) picked kernel K in the last 200ms, bias +0.15 to K's score.

Jordan: Agreed. Quick patch suggestion:
```patch
- score = base_score(candidate)
+ score = base_score(candidate) + sticky_bias(candidate, recent_window_ms=200, bias=0.15)
```
This should keep sticky behavior for short bursts but still allow long-term switches.

Aisha: For immediate mitigation, can we pin the canary to force flash_v3_causal for that model? Or temporarily widen padbucketizer boundaries so 512 picks v3? Pinning seems safer.

Sara K.: I pushed a canary pin to force v3 on canary-11 for the impacted model and rolled out a tiny config tweak to padbucketizer to avoid the 512 boundary. Observed p50 drop back to baseline in the next 30s.

ci-deploy-bot: Deploy started: patch/pin/canary-11 by sara.k.101
ci-deploy-bot: Deploy succeeded: patch/pin/canary-11 (3 nodes) in 41s

Mike L.: Nice. Follow-ups: 1) add sticky_bias experiment and run perf sweep across head_dim in {8,12,16,20,24,32} x seqlen {128,256,512,1024}; 2) add a short-term KV warmup flag to the profiler so we can correlate prefetch decisions with kv_state; 3) add a unit test for padbucketizer boundaries.

Jordan: I'll draft the PR for sticky_bias and the test. Aisha — can you add the kv_state trace bits to rb-runtime profiler?

Aisha: On it, will post a draft by EOD.

Sara K.: Leaving logs and the repro script in the runtime-debug s3 bucket: s3://redwood-runtime/debug/3321123456/canary-11-repro.tar.gz 

Mike L.: Great thread — thanks all. :thumbsup:
